body:
Seems that the shape `(500, 1, 5, 3400)` is reshaped here to `(500, 80, 5, 3400)` then ascontiguousarray is called. I wonder why it runs on WSL2 machine without the same OoM.
https://github.com/cupy/cupy/blob/64387fa95d339127b76b81d8459ffca5d2e28bc1/cupy/_core/_gufuncs.py#L468-L473

The behavior on WSL2 was also quite strange.

I tried follow the error message stack I got from generic Ubuntu and set a breakpoint in `cupy._core._gufuncs` on WSL2 Ubuntu. (I use vscode for breakpoint)
WSL2 will also hit the out-of-memory error if the breakpoint in `cupy` is active,
and if I deactivate the breakpoint, the code works again (in WSL2).
This is not just same system running two different OSs, but two different systems with different drivers, CUDA Toolkits, and even GPUs. I am not sure what's the point of comparison?

Ah, sry i wasn't aware of that.
I tried different cuda and driver versions on generic ubuntu and they all failed.
(Combinations of: OS 18.04, 22.04; cuda 11.8, 12.1, 12.3; drivers 520, 530, 545. No change on GPU though, always 1050ti with generic Ubuntu)
(more edit: i forgot that i also tried w/ OS 20.04, cuda 12.3, driver 545 on 3090ti, generic Ubuntu. It also failed, except I need to use larger `s0, s1, s2, s3`).

Essentially i was hoping `ab_bad = cp.matmul(a_bad, b_bad)` would also work on generic Ubuntu.
I assumed that the failed `matmul` was unnecessarily mallocating for the element-wise multiplication step of a matmul, before the reduce summation step.
Then I found that probably wasn't the case since it worked on WSL2.
So I thought there was maybe a flag that prevented `cupy` on generic Ubuntu from smartly handling the matmul w/o a ridiculous malloc, and something could be done about it...

To me, the main issue here is the somewhat ridiculous memory footprint of `cupy.matmul` in cases where unnecessary mallocates could have been avoided if the axes of operands were ordered properly.

Here's a helper function covers up the issue with some automatic `transpose` and `reshape`.
(Probably not bug-free).
I guess such array-massaging should ideally be inside `matmul` or somewhere else in `cupy`, but I lack the expertise to directly patch for it...
```py
import cupy as cp


def matmul_helper(
    a: cp.ndarray,
    b: cp.ndarray,
) -> cp.ndarray:
    ## preprocessing
    orig_a_shape, orig_b_shape = a.shape, b.shape
    length = a.shape[-1]

    # match ndim
    ndim_diff = a.ndim - b.ndim
    ndim = max(a.ndim, b.ndim)

    if ndim_diff > 0:
        b = b.reshape(ndim_diff*(1,)+b.shape)
    elif ndim_diff < 0:
        a = a.reshape(-ndim_diff*(1,)+a.shape)

    a_shape, b_shape = a.shape, b.shape

    # broadcastable?
    broadcastable = all(
        ((sa == sb) or sa == 1 or sb == 1) for (sa, sb) in
        zip(a_shape[:-2], b_shape[:-2])
    )
    if (not broadcastable) or (a_shape[-1] != b_shape[-2]):
        raise ValueError(f'Imcompatible shapes: {orig_a_shape, orig_b_shape}')

    # transpose
    dims_shared = tuple(_ for _ in range(ndim-2) if a_shape[_] == b_shape[_])
    dims_matmul = tuple(_ for _ in range(ndim-2) if a_shape[_] != b_shape[_])
    ndim_shared = len(dims_shared)
    ndim_matmul = len(dims_matmul)

    old2new_axes_order = dims_shared + dims_matmul + (ndim-2, ndim-1)
    new2old_axes_order = tuple(
        i[0] for i in sorted(enumerate(old2new_axes_order), key=lambda x:x[1])
    )  # `cupy.argsort` can't handle `tuple` input

    a = a.transpose(old2new_axes_order)
    b = b.transpose(dims_shared + (ndim-2,) + dims_matmul + (ndim-1,))

    shared_shape = a.shape[:ndim_shared]
    a_unique_shape = a.shape[ndim_shared:-1]
    b_unique_shape = b.shape[ndim_shared+1:]

    ab = cp.matmul(
        a.reshape(shared_shape + (-1, length)),
        b.reshape(shared_shape + (length, -1)),
    ).reshape(shared_shape + a_unique_shape + b_unique_shape)

    # Move all size-1 dim to the end, notice that either `_a == 1` or `_b == 1`
    # for `(_a, _b) in zip(a_unique_shape[:-1], b_unique_shape[:-1])`.
    choose_a = tuple(
        _a > _b for (_a, _b) in zip(a_unique_shape[:-1], b_unique_shape[:-1])
    )

    offset_a = ndim_shared
    offset_b = offset_a + ndim_matmul + 1
    ndim_ab = ab.ndim

    a_range = range(offset_a, offset_a + ndim_matmul + 1)
    b_range = range(offset_b, offset_b + ndim_matmul + 1)

    shared_axes = tuple(range(ndim_shared))
    axes_left = tuple(
        _a if _ else _b for (_, _a, _b) in zip(choose_a, a_range, b_range)
    )
    axes_right = tuple(
        _b if _ else _a for (_, _a, _b) in zip(choose_a, a_range, b_range)
    )
    ab_axes = shared_axes + axes_left + (offset_b-1, ndim_ab-1) + axes_right

    ab = ab.transpose(ab_axes).squeeze(axis=tuple(range(offset_b+1, ndim_ab)))

    ab = ab.transpose(new2old_axes_order)
    return ab


if __name__ == '__main__':
    s0, s1, s2, s3 = 2, 3, 5, 4
    a = cp.random.rand(s0, 1, s3, s2)
    b = cp.random.rand(s0, s1, s2, 1)

    ab_ref = cp.matmul(a, b)
    ab = matmul_helper(a, b)
    print(f'a, b, ab_ref, ab: {a.shape, b.shape, ab_ref.shape, ab.shape}')
    print(f'(ab - ab_ref).(max, min): {(ab-ab_ref).max(), (ab-ab_ref).min()}')

```
